findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, opinions_list, bills_list, code_browse, constitution_browse, meetings_lookup, meetings_get_transcript, meetings_list, meetings_search · Private data: search, fetch, verify_quote, opinions_lookup, opinions_search, bills_lookup, bills_search, code_search, meetings_lookup, meetings_for_bill · Public sink: opinions_lookup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, opinions_list, bills_list, code_browse, constitution_browse, meetings_lookup, meetings_get_transcript, meetings_list, meetings_search · Private data: search, fetch, verify_quote, opinions_lookup, opinions_search, bills_lookup, bills_search, code_search, meetings_lookup, meetings_for_bill · Public sink: opinions_lookup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "describe_site" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
